channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Dívida pública avança sob Lula, que transfere bomba fiscal para a próxima gestão
item.description: Brazil's public debt rose to 79% of GDP in 2024, up from 72% in 2023, and is projected to reach 88% by 2029 under optimistic government forecasts that independent analysts deem unrealistic. Despite criticizing Bolsonaro's 'fiscal inheritance,' the Lula administration has expanded spending amid high interest rates and primary deficits, creating a 'fiscal bomb' to be passed to the next government. This rising debt increases country risk, diverts capital from productive investment to public bonds, and threatens long-term growth.

item.title: SP cria Plano de Segurança Viária para reduzir mortes no trânsito
item.description: The São Paulo state government instituted the State Road Safety Plan (PSV-SP) aiming to cut traffic deaths by half within five years, aligned with Vision Zero and Safe System principles. The plan establishes a Steering Committee, provides technical support to municipalities, enhances enforcement through technology and data management, and prioritizes vulnerable road users, especially motorcyclists, via initiatives like the 'Mão na Roda' program.

item.title: Risco país volta para o menor patamar no governo Lula
item.description: Brazil's country risk (5-year CDS) closed at 122.9 points on April 24, 2026, matching the lowest level under President Lula’s government, recorded in February 2024. The decline signals improved investor confidence despite domestic fiscal and political uncertainties, occurring amid a global environment of increased risk appetite and dollar weakness. The indicator, which had peaked at 279.65 points in March 2023, has shown substantial recovery since then.

item.title: Governo critica taxa das blusinhas por causa da eleição, diz associação
item.description: Edmundo Lima, executive director of ABVTex, criticized the federal government for discussing the repeal of the 'blusinhas tax' during an election year, claiming it is motivated by image recovery rather than economic justification. He argued for maintaining the tax to ensure fair competition between domestic retailers and international platforms, warning that its removal could lead to store closures and the loss of millions of jobs.

item.title: Entre medidas sociais e de segurança, Lula ainda precisa vencer debate da corrupção
item.description: The Lula government plans to launch in May new social and security measures, including actions against femicide, crime, and the Desenrola 2 program for indebted individuals, aiming to reverse declining popularity. Despite these efforts, Lula still faces the central challenge of overcoming corruption perceptions that affect his image. The article notes these initiatives are part of a broader strategy to regain electoral support ahead of the 2026 political landscape.

item.title: Nunes Marques quer aperfeiçoar cerco a uso indevido de inteligência artificial nas campanhas
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, who will assume the presidency of the TSE in May, aims to strengthen controls against the improper use of AI in the 2026 electoral campaigns, focusing on combating AI-generated disinformation. He plans to set deadlines for big techs to submit compliance plans, meet with their representatives, maintain ongoing dialogue, unify disciplinary processes, and reinforce confidence in the electronic voting system to depoliticize the electoral environment.

item.title: PL avalia que Zema ‘radical’ perde força para ser vice de Flávio
item.description: PL leaders argue that Romeu Zema's radicalization, particularly his attacks on the STF and controversial remarks about the Northeast, weakens his viability as Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate, as the senator needs to appeal to centrist voters. The party plans to test alternative candidates in polls, including Tereza Cristina, Simone Marchetto, Clarissa Tércio, and Priscila Costa, to balance the ticket and improve Northeastern prospects.

item.title: STF e a questão democrática
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court faces legitimate criticism over alleged conflicts of interest involving justices and their families, particularly tied to the Banco Master scandal, but institutional attacks on the Court in the context of coup attempts require collective defense. A proposed ethical code of conduct, championed by Court President Edson Fachin and drafted by Minister Cármen Lúcia, is seen as the best remedy to restore credibility, while generic or opportunistic critiques, such as those from Romeu Zema, are dismissed.

item.title: Arco-íris em Nuvens de Chumbo: a resistência da civilidade no século XXI
item.description: The text describes an alarming rise in hate speech, intolerance, and disinformation in Brazil and globally, including racism, antisemitism, homophobia, misogyny, xenophobia, and aporophobia, often linked to authoritarian and denialist movements attacking social rights, science, and democracy. Civilized values are eroding, with empathy replaced by hatred and dehumanization used as a political tactic, echoing patterns seen in the rise of Nazism.

item.title: Freada de arrumação
item.description: The dispute between candidate Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais, and Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes is opening space for an alternative candidacy to the polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. While Lula seeks to unite the nation against coupism, Flávio attempts to approach the moderate right or center, leveraging Brazil’s historically conservative and centrist electorate, which has long defined election outcomes.

item.title: Indicado ao STF, Jorge Messias passa por sabatina da CCJ do Senado na próxima quarta-feira; entenda como funciona
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias will undergo a hearing before the Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee next Wednesday (29) as part of his nomination to fill a vacancy on the Supreme Federal Court left by Justice Luís Roberto Barroso's retirement. Committee rapporteur Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA) has already issued a favorable opinion. Approval requires an absolute majority of senators — at least 41 out of 81.

item.title: Entrevista: lulismo enfrenta 'crise de criatividade' para lidar com jovens, diz Preto Zezé, presidente da Cufa
item.description: Preto Zezé, president of Cufa, states that Lulism faces a 'creativity crisis' for failing to meet young Brazilians' demands for autonomy and concrete future prospects. He argues that youth are distancing themselves from traditional politics due to frustration with unfulfilled promises of social mobility and stability, amid a broader context of crisis and institutional distrust.

item.title: 'Sacrifícios pessoais' e 'necessaire política': como é a cartilha do PL que ensina mulheres a disputar as eleições
item.description: PL Mulher, led by Michelle Bolsonaro, provides a training guide for women seeking to run for office, emphasizing self-knowledge, electoral strategy, and personal sacrifices. The program includes the 'PL Mulher compass,' which positions the family as the political north, and initiatives like the Alicerça Brazil Project and the 'political necessaire,' distributed at events with practical guidance for first-time candidates.

item.title: Messias dribla ausência da Alcolumbre e tenta acelerar conversas com senadores às vésperas de sabatina pré-STF
item.description: Jorge Messias, AGU minister and STF nominee, intensifies talks with senators ahead of his CCJ confirmation hearing, addressing issues like Banco Master, abortion, and Judiciary-Legislature relations. Despite speaking with around 75 senators, the absence of Senate President Davi Alcolumbre raises concerns. His strategy emphasizes a moderate, institutional tone to avoid congressional confrontation and gain 46–48 favorable votes, particularly by supporting legislative handling of abortion expansion.

item.title: Entrevista: 'Se o STF decidir, o TRE-RJ está preparado para eleição direta', afirma presidente do tribunal
item.description: The president of the TRE-RJ, Judge Claudio de Mello Tavares, states that the court is prepared to conduct a direct election for state governor if the STF so rules. He also emphasizes increased scrutiny of candidacies linked to organized crime and in high-risk areas across Rio de Janeiro. The interview is exclusive to GLOBO subscribers.

item.title: Motorista dono de perfil alvo de ação do PT nega ser bolsonarista e diz faturar R$ 1,5 mil por mês com personagem de IA
item.description: Daniel Cristiano dos Santos, an app driver and owner of the Dona Maria AI-generated profile criticizing the Lula government, denies being a Bolsonarist and claims to earn R$1,500 monthly from the content. The profile was targeted by the PT, PV, and PC do B in Electoral Justice for alleged premature election propaganda via deepfake, despite the AI origin being disclosed in the description. Santos says he supports candidates like Romeu Zema (Novo) and Abilio Brunini, and has campaigned for Bolsonaro’s son in potential runoff scenarios.

item.title: Mandato, código de ética: o que pré-candidatos defendem para o STF
item.description: As 2026 elections approach, presidential pre-candidates are advocating for STF reforms amid a credibility crisis linked to the Banco Master scandal. Lula (PT) supports term limits for justices and a code of conduct, while Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) endorses impeachment of STF ministers as a accountability measure.

item.title: Eleitor tem 10 dias para regularizar título para votar em 2026
item.description: Brazilian voters have until May 6 to regularize their voter ID and ensure their right to vote in the 2026 elections. The deadline applies to those whose IDs were canceled due to failure to vote, justify absence, or pay fines in three consecutive elections, as well as first-time applicants. The first round of the 2026 elections is scheduled for October 4, with a potential runoff on October 25.

item.title: PECs da escala 6x1 não passam de oportunismo
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in committee two PECs that would abolish the 6x1 work schedule, driven by the government via an urgent bill, aiming for a plenary vote by May. The rush, dictated by the electoral calendar, limits substantive debate and risks negative economic consequences. The article warns of political opportunism and irresponsibility in discussing labor reform.

item.title: Congresso Nacional analisa veto de Lula ao PL da Dosimetria; saiba o que está em jogo
item.description: Congress is set to review, on Thursday (30), President Lula's veto of the 'Dosimetria Bill,' which reduces penalties for crimes such as violent abolition of the democratic state and coup d'état, potentially benefiting those convicted in the January 8 attacks and allies of former President Bolsonaro. The bill prevents cumulative sentencing when crimes occur in the same context, applying the 'formal concurrence of crimes' rule, and further reduces punishment in crowd-related offenses if no leadership or financing is involved. Overriding the veto requires an absolute majority in both the Chamber (257 deputies) and Senate (41 senators), voted separately.

item.title: Zema fez as pazes com a Inconfidência Mineira, mas já a viu com outros olhos
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema commented on the anniversary of Tiradentes' execution, stating that Brasília exploits Brazil as the Portuguese did, and emphasized that the struggle of the Inconfidência Mineira is not over. His remarks were seen as a critique of federal power and an attempt to re-engage with the symbolism of the Inconfidência Mineira following previous controversies.

item.title: Clãs familiares testam força nas urnas e buscam retomar protagonismo
item.description: Brazil's major political family clans are preparing for the October 2026 elections, aiming to regain their prominence in a context of strong national polarization and competitive state-level races. Traditional surnames are returning to the ballot to test the electoral strength of their legacy in a highly contested political environment.

item.title: Terceira via acumula derrotas, e ex-presidenciáveis se voltam para eleições estaduais
item.description: Historically, candidates who finished in third place in Brazilian presidential elections since redemocratization in 1989 have never been elected president in subsequent attempts. After these defeats, many of these former presidential contenders, often associated with the 'third way', redirected their political ambitions to state-level elections. This pattern reflects the difficulty of overcoming the effective two-party dominance in Brazil's presidential races.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio dizem que Zema aumentou cacife para ser vice, após embate com STF
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro claim that the confrontation between Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema (Novo) and STF justices, particularly Gilmar Mendes, has boosted his political standing to be chosen as vice on the senator’s PL ticket. The maneuver suggests that visibility gained from the judiciary clash strengthens his position as a potential vice-presidential candidate in 2026.

item.title: Flávio diz que 'Pix é nosso' e que vai negociar com os EUA em novo vídeo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) released a pre-campaign presidential video on social media stating 'Pix is ours' and that he would negotiate with the United States if elected. The video was published on April 25, 2026, emphasizing his economic and foreign policy stance.

item.title: “O Pix é nosso e sem taxa”, diz Flávio em novo vídeo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) claims the Pix is a national pride and will remain fee-free, linking its creation to his father Jair Bolsonaro’s government and highlighting the banking inclusion of over 68 million people. He criticizes rising prices, advocates prioritizing higher education funding in technology and AI, and proposes a pragmatic foreign policy with the U.S. and China, urging Brazil to add value to its exports rather than raw commodity sales.

item.title: Zema vê “xenofobia” em fala de Gilmar e cogita ação judicial
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor and Novo party presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema said he is considering legal action against Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes for remarks he labeled 'xenophobic' regarding his accent. The comments were made during an interview at the opening of Expozebu in Uberaba, prompting Zema to call them offensive and disrespectful.

item.title: Caiado diz que eleitor escolherá quem vai ao 2º turno e pede convergência
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pré-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) stated that voters will decide who advances to the second round of the 2026 elections and urged convergence among opposition candidates. He emphasized the need for unity to strengthen the alternative to the current federal government, without specifying particular alliances.

item.title: Sem citar Lula, Tarcísio diz que há 'lideranças envelhecidas' que não percebem a hora de parar
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) stated that there are 'aged leaders' in Brazil who fail to recognize it is time to step down, without explicitly naming President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. He added it is 'time to give way' and reiterated his bid for re-election in the 2026 São Paulo gubernatorial race.

item.title: Zema diz que é preciso renovar o Judiciário; 'a corrupção está correndo solta', afirma
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) called for structural reforms of the Brazilian Judiciary, stating that corruption is 'running loose'. Speaking at the opening of Expozebu in Uberaba (MG), he emphasized the need for systemic changes and stricter measures against corruption and crime.

item.title: Autofagia dos irmãos mastiga suposta moderação de Flávio
item.description: Bolsonaro's sons are criticizing allies for alleged lack of commitment to their brother Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, using the metaphor of 'autophagy' to describe those who do not sufficiently support the candidacy. This suggests internal tension within the Bolsonaro orbit, where loyalty is being tested ahead of the 2026 presidential succession.

item.title: Zema retoma ataques ao STF com vídeo de IA e ironiza pedido de inclusão no inquérito das fake news por Gilmar
item.description: Romeu Zema resumed his attacks on the Supreme Court in an AI-generated puppet video, mocking Gilmar Mendes’ request to include him in the fake news inquiry. He labeled ministers as 'untouchables' and 'rotten fruits', accusing them of abusing power for personal gain and citing alleged ties to businessman Daniel Vorcaro. Zema also linked the judiciary to national conflicts and reiterated his electoral stance against the 'powerful'.

item.title: Bolsonaro aguarda autorização do “ministro médico” Moraes para cirurgia, diz Carluxo
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro (PL), pre-candidate for Senate from Santa Catarina, visited his father, Jair Bolsonaro (PL), in Brasília on Saturday, the 25th. After the meeting, Carlos stated that the former president is awaiting authorization from Minister Alexandre de Moraes for shoulder surgery, which 'bothers him quite a bit'. The term 'minister doctor' is used ironically, reflecting criticism of the Supreme Court justice.

item.title: Quaest divulga rodada de pesquisas sobre eleição de governadores a partir de segunda
item.description: Quaest will release starting Monday (27) a round of polls showing the state of gubernatorial races in 11 states, including São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Minas Gerais, with scenarios for first and second rounds and Senate vote intentions. The polls also include presidential race questions, featuring 12 pre-candidates, including Ciro Gomes, who has not yet decided on a presidential run. The national Quaest poll from April 15 showed Lula at 37%, Flávio Bolsonaro at 32%, Ronaldo Caiado at 6%, and Romeu Zema at 3%.

item.title: "Dona Maria": PT aciona TSE contra perfil criado por IA para atacar Lula
item.description: The Brazil of Hope Federation (PT, PV, and PCdoB) filed a complaint with the TSE requesting the suspension of the 'Dona Maria' social media profiles, claiming they use an AI-generated character to spread disinformation against President Lula, praise Bolsonaro, and attack the Supreme Court. The profile, with 724k Instagram followers, is run by Daniel Cristiano, who called the action 'desperation'.

item.title: Problema de foco afasta Lula do eleitorado feminino
item.description: Women's support for Lula is gradually declining, despite still exceeding the national average, according to Genial/Quaest and Datafolha polls. The government has attempted to regain this electorate through initiatives like the national pact against femicide, signing protective laws, and recreating the Ministry of Women, but experts argue that the lack of focus on concrete actions in security, health, and education is driving away the female vote, which represents a crucial electoral advantage due to its majority in the electorate.

item.title: Zema ironiza Gilmar, Moraes e voos em jatinhos em novo vídeo
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo-MG) released a video satirizing STF ministers Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes, using AI-generated puppets to criticize his inclusion in the fake news inquiry and referencing the Banco Master case and flights on aircraft linked to Daniel Vorcaro. The video is part of his 'Os Intocáveis' series, which he uses to respond to what he describes as institutional persecution.

item.title: Sem citar Flávio, Tarcísio chama Lula de ultrapassado e defende renovação
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized President Lula, calling him an 'aged and outdated' leader with nothing left to offer, and called for political renewal. Although he did not directly mention Flávio Bolsonaro, his remarks align with the opposition's discourse against the federal government. The statement was made amid growing polarization between the São Paulo state government and the federal executive.

item.title: Zema publica novo vídeo com fantoches de Gilmar e Moraes
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pré-candidate for the Novo party, published a new video in his 'Os Intocáveis' series satirizing Supreme Court ministers Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes, depicted as puppets. The fifth episode in the sequence was shared on social media on Saturday, the 25th, and forms part of his broader critique of the Brazilian judiciary.

item.title: Sem citar Lula, Tarcísio diz que há ‘lideranças envelhecidas’ que não percebem a hora de parar
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas stated that there are 'aged leaderships' in Brazil that fail to recognize it's time to step aside and allow for renewal, without directly naming President Lula. He emphasized the need for political renewal and acknowledged that he too will one day have to leave office.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pede unidade da direita após atrito entre Nikolas e Jair Renan
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro appealed for unity on the right via social media following renewed public tensions between federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira and councilman Jair Renan Bolsonaro, son of the former president. He criticized internal provocations and urged focus on countering left-wing opposition, stating that support is earned, not imposed. The statement came after Nikolas insulted Jair Renan's cognitive capacity in a post on X.

item.title: O lugar de Flávio Bolsonaro na história de truques e estelionatos eleitorais do Brasil
item.description: The article discusses Flávio Bolsonaro's role in electoral fraud schemes in Brazil, comparing him to historical practices of political and financial manipulation, such as those seen during the Collor government. It suggests that Bolsonaro is part of a tradition of using illegal tactics to gain electoral advantage, linking this to concerns about asset confiscation and economic instability.

item.title: Bolsonaro espera decisão do "ministro médico Moraes", diz Carlos
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro announced that his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, is awaiting authorization from Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes to undergo shoulder surgery, following three consecutive pneumonias. The request has already been filed and received support from the Prosecutor General's Office. Carlos also revealed that Jair Bolsonaro is finalizing a list of Senate pre-candidates for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Moro e Flávio aparecem juntos pela 1ª vez em vídeo do PL
item.description: The Paraná branch of the Liberal Party (PL) released a video featuring the first joint appearance of Flávio Bolsonaro and Sergio Moro, the party's pre-candidates for president and governor of Paraná, alongside Filipe Barros. The ad emphasizes the party's growth in the state, pledges to protect Paraná and oppose 'petists and criminals', and reinforces a hardline stance against the left and corruption. Moro, who left União Brasil to join the PL in March 2026 after conflicts with the PP, seeks to rebrand himself as a loyal Bolsonaro ally following his contentious resignation from the federal government in 2020.

item.title: PT recorre a nomes históricos para puxar voto para a Câmara
item.description: The PT is turning to historical figures such as José Dirceu, João Paulo Cunha, and Delúbio Soares to strengthen its presence in the Chamber of Deputies in 2026, betting on their experience and national recognition. Dirceu is running for a federal deputy seat in São Paulo after his convictions were annulled, Cunha left the private sector to return to politics with direct support from Lula, and Delúbio Soares is running again in Goiás after recovering his political rights, stating he would make the same choices again despite the Mensalão scandal.

item.title: Carlos Bolsonaro fala em 'oportunistas' após critica de Nikolas Ferreira: 'Brasil merece mais'
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro (PL-SC) criticized fellow bolsonarists as 'opportunists' for not promoting his brother Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, asserting that political loyalty should not be based on convenience. He emphasized that the movement must uphold its principles and that Brazil deserves better than current internal divisions. The remarks follow a public exchange with Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG), who argued that electoral success comes from substantive ideas and effort, not merely social media activity.

item.title: Lideranças do agronegócio criticam fim da escala 6x1 na abertura da Expozebu
item.description: Agribusiness leaders criticized the Lula government's proposal to end the 6x1 work schedule during the opening of Expozebu in Uberaba, MG. They argue the change could harm productivity and workers' rights in rural areas.

item.title: Eleições 2026: após atrito entre Nikolas e Jair Renan, Flávio Bolsonaro pede unidade da direita
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) called for unity on the right following tensions between Nikolas Ferreira and Jair Renan Bolsonaro, urging cohesion among Bolsonaro allies ahead of the 2026 elections. He published an appeal to the base, criticizing internal provocations that weaken the conservative camp.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pede fim de cobranças entre aliados do PL
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) called for an end to provocations among Bolsonarist allies after exchanges of insults between Nikolas Ferreira and Jair Renan Bolsonaro. He emphasized that support must be earned, not imposed, and that each person contributes at their own pace, stressing the need for unity to win the 2026 elections.

item.title: “Tá na hora de largar o osso e sair”, diz Tarcísio sobre Lula
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized Brazil's aging political leadership without naming names directly, calling for renewal and suggesting some leaders fail to recognize when it's time to step down. Although he did not explicitly mention Lula in the excerpt, the post's title associates his remarks with a critique of the president, implying Lula is among those referenced. The comments were made during an event in Monteiro Lobato, in the countryside of São Paulo.
